entities.summary: Carrick-on-Shannon is the county town of County Leitrim in Ireland. It is the largest town in the county. A smaller part of the town located on the west bank of the River Shannon lies in County Roscommon and is home to the town's main train station. As of the 2022 census, the population of the town was 4,743. It is situated on a strategic crossing point of the River Shannon. The main part of the town, the County Leitrim part, is in the civil parish of Kiltoghert, which is in the barony of Leitrim, while Cortober, which is the County Roscommon side of the town, is in the civil parish of Killukin, in the barony of Boyle.

historicalSignificance.significanceNarrative: As a strategic crossing point of the River Shannon, Carrick-on-Shannon has played a significant role in Ireland's transportation and trade networks since ancient times. The town's population has grown steadily over the centuries, with the 2022 census reporting 4,743 residents.
